builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
summary: The paper replaces text-only Chinese grammatical error correction with G-CGEC, an image-to-grounded-edit task that requires corrections and their visual positions on handwritten essay images. It costs added pipeline or multi-agent orchestration, OCR and character-grounding components, more latency, and dependence on proprietary or open VLM quality rather than a single deployable model. It can fail because top proprietary models perform poorly in single pass, while linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding remain the primary bottlenecks.
rationale: This is relevant to applied education AI and multi-component VLM systems, but the benchmark is specialized, the strongest result depends on auxiliary OCR, grounding, and agent coordination, and the abstract gives no deployable small-model recipe or quantified efficiency gain for a constrained production stack.
technique: Agentic and pipelined vision-language workflows for grounded Chinese GEC

claims.statement: The paper replaces text-only Chinese grammatical error correction with G-CGEC, an image-to-grounded-edit task that requires corrections and their visual positions on handwritten essay images. It costs added pipeline or multi-agent orchestration, OCR and character-grounding components, more latency, and dependence on proprietary or open VLM quality rather than a single deployable model. It can fail because top proprietary models perform poorly in single pass, while linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding remain the primary bottlenecks.

Pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements over direct single-pass vision-language models, with an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieving the best benchmark performance; no multiplicative factor is reported in the abstract.
